question.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)={y}^{3}\,i+(2+x)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & ={y}^{3}=8{sin}^{3}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =2+x=2+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $\operatorname{sin}⁡t=u,du=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(8{sin}^{3}⁡t)\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(2+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }16{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t+16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }16{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{0}16{u}^{3}+16u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t{|}_{0}^{2\pi }+0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
